property_summary: For any caller and any timestamp, when fallback is called with exactly 10 ether the reference contract always updates pastBlockTime to the current block.timestamp (so subsequent getter returns that timestamp); the mutant requiring 11 ether prevents this for calls sending 10 ether, so there exist inputs (amount == 10 ether) where pastBlockTime is not updated.

For any caller and block timestamp, if fallback is invoked with exactly 10 ether the reference contract updates pastBlockTime to the current block.timestamp (so the public getter pastBlockTime equals block.timestamp after the call); the mutant requiring 11 ether prevents this for calls sending 10 ether and thus can leave pastBlockTime unchanged.

For any caller and block time, when the contract's fallback is invoked with exactly 10 ether the reference contract always accepts the call and updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp (so getter pastBlockTime equals block.timestamp); the mutant that requires 11 ether will reject calls of 10 ether and thus can leave pastBlockTime unchanged, violating this rule for inputs where amount == 10 ether.

For every caller and block timestamp, if fallback is invoked with any ether amount equal to 10 ether the reference contract accepts the call and updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp (so the public getter pastBlockTime equals block.timestamp); the mutant that requires 11 ether will reject calls sending 10 ether and thus can leave pastBlockTime unchanged, violating this rule for those inputs.

For any caller and block.timestamp, whenever the fallback is invoked with an amount NOT equal to 11 ether and that call succeeds on the reference contract, the reference contract's pastBlockTime becomes equal to block.timestamp after the call; the mutant (which requires 11 ether) will reject or not update pastBlockTime for some such amounts (e.g., 10 ether), so there exist inputs where the property fails on the mutant.

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether to the fallback, the reference contract always updates pastBlockTime to the current block.timestamp after the call (so pastBlockTime == block.timestamp), whereas the mutant inverts the timestamp check and thus can prevent updating pastBlockTime for some inputs making pastBlockTime remain greater than or equal to block.timestamp (i.e., not equal to block.timestamp) after the call.

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether to C's fallback, the reference contract always sets pastBlockTime to the current block.timestamp after the call; the mutant that requires block.timestamp < pastBlockTime can cause pastBlockTime to NOT become equal to block.timestamp for some (fuzzed) prior pastBlockTime / block.timestamp conditions, so there exist inputs where the mutant violates that equality.

For any call that sends exactly 10 ether to C.fallback, the reference contract always sets pastBlockTime to the current block.timestamp after the call; the mutant that inverts the timestamp check can (for some prior pastBlockTime and current block.timestamp) reject the update so pastBlockTime != block.timestamp afterwards.
